comments.text:
For some reasons, I need to define a function, like the one below. In reality, both the parameters and the body of the function are much more complex than this example.
```
myfun <- function(method, insert, signature = NULL){
  # Other code
  trace(method, tracer = insert, signature = signature)
  # Other code
}
```

Then I create S3 and S4 methods with the same body, simulating the real-life scenario encountered.
```
# For S3
S3Fun <- function(x){ UseMethod("S3Fun") }
S3Fun.default <- function(x){
  .local <- function(x){
    x
  }
  .local(x)
}

# For S4
setGeneric("S4Fun", function(x) standardGeneric("S4Fun"))
setMethod("S4Fun", "ANY", function(x){
  .local <- function(x){
    x
  }
  .local(x)
})
```

Next, I will proceed with the following steps:
```
# For S3
myfun("S3Fun.default", insert = quote(message("tracing ...")))
S3Fun(1)

# For S4
myfun("S4Fun", insert = quote(message("tracing ...")), signature = "ANY")
S4Fun(1)
```

You will find that "S3Fun" produces the expected result, while "S4Fun" throws an error.
```
# For S4
Error in eval(expr, p) : object 'insert' not found
```

I believe that "trace()" as a fundamental function should not produce such differences on S3 and S4. Therefore, I consider this to be a potential bug.

I checked the source code of the "trace()" method and found that the problem occurred in this code in the "`methods:::.TraceWithMethods()`" method:
```
if (isRematched(def)) {
  expr <- substitute(trace(.local, tracer = tr, at = at,
                           exit = ex, print = pr, edit = ed, where = sys.frame(sys.nframe())),
                     list(tr = substitute(tracer), ex = exit, at = at, pr = print, ed = edit))
  at <- 3L
  tracer <- expr
  print <- FALSE
}
```

I think the 'substitute()' function should not be used here. When I change "`substitute(tracer)`" to just "`tracer`", the issue is indeed resolved.

I think this segment of code should be modified to:
```
if (isRematched(def)) {
  expr <- substitute(trace(.local, tracer = tr, at = at,
                           exit = ex, print = pr, edit = ed, where = sys.frame(sys.nframe())),
                     list(tr = tracer, ex = exit, at = at, pr = print, ed = edit))
  at <- 3L
  tracer <- expr
  print <- FALSE
}
```

comments.creator: jaganmn2
comments.text: Yes, `tr=substitute(tracer)` is wrong, but so are `tr=tracer` and `ex=exit`, because the case `is.function(.)` must be handled specially, according to `is.name(substitute(.))` in the current frame.  I am testing a different patch.
